description: Issue #746, the profile-INACTIVE direction: byte-for-byte the same source as `reserved-reporters-with-sprites`, checked under Core + Turtle & Rendering alone, is completely clean. Without `sprites` claimed the reporters register nothing (`collectVisibleNames` gates them on the profile), so `new_turtle`/`who`/`turtles` are ordinary names a program is free to declare — mirroring `reserved-procedures-without-sprites`, which does the same for the block-heads. SCOPE, CORRECTED: maintainer ruling #833 retracted that gate for the NAMING axis. `spec/grammar.md:408` makes every profile's primitives built-in names unconditionally -- what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it -- so a conforming 0.4.0 implementation must raise `ol-reserved-word` on these three declarations with or without the profile. `spec/tooling.md:175-176` is about which names are AVAILABLE (the `ol-unknown-command` axis) and does not gate the reserved-word rule; the earlier reading of it here conflated the two axes. This fixture therefore pins SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR the spec now contradicts, and is kept red-flagged rather than deleted so the behaviour is not silently unpinned; issue #841 flips this expectation. Note this is a bare *declaration*: the `ol-unknown-command` a **call** to one of these names raises under Core-only is a different rule, covered by `sprites/reporters-unknown-without-sprites`. Sharing one source with the rejecting sibling is deliberate, so the two cannot diverge and silently stop testing the gate. `"check": true` for the same reason as the sibling: this is a checker rule with no execution.
